# External detection corpus

Full analytic rules are kept as authored. The v1 grammars accept a prefix of each rule (KQL `where` pipes before `summarize` assignments; SPL after a leading macro when the search is a field comparison). `external_corpus.rs` injects `frobnicate` or `notacommand` on that prefix and requires the unknown-operator or unknown-command diagnostic. The broken full file must also produce at least one diagnostic.

Queries are extracted from public detection content for conformance.
Each broken file is the same query with one injected fault.

## ES|QL, EQL, Lucene — SigmaHQ/sigma (Detection Rule License 1.1)

SigmaHQ rules at `SigmaHQ/sigma@05d1031f537e830b76da53bae2400c5814c89165`, converted with `pysigma-backend-elasticsearch` 2.1.1 (pySigma 1.5.1, no processing pipeline, so Sigma field names are kept) by its `ESQLBackend`, `EqlBackend`, and `LuceneBackend`. The converted queries are modified forms of the rules, shared under the Detection Rule License 1.1: [`LICENSE.DRL-1.1.md`](LICENSE.DRL-1.1.md). Each `.broken.` twin is the same query with one injected fault: ES|QL `| where` becomes `| frobnicate`, EQL `where` becomes `wehre`, and Lucene gains an unbalanced `(`. `sigma.tsv` is the machine-readable list.

Elastic's own prebuilt rules (`elastic/detection-rules`) are Elastic License 2.0 and are not vendored; `crates/opentide-analysis/tests/elastic_detection_rules.rs` reads them from a checkout.

### Lucene, Carbon Black Cloud

The same SigmaHQ commit, converted with `pysigma-backend-carbonblack` 0.1.14 (MIT; pySigma 1.5.1) and its `CarbonBlack_pipeline`, which maps Sigma fields to Carbon Black Cloud process search fields, by `scripts/engine/sigma_carbon_black_corpus.py`: the first eight rules (by path) that convert in each of `process_creation`, `image_load`, `file_event`, `network_connection` and `registry_set`. They are in `lucene-carbon-black/`, checked in the Carbon Black dialect (`crates/opentide-lucene/tests/external_carbon_black.rs`). Each `.broken.` twin gains an unbalanced `(`.

## Lucene parser tests — apache/lucene (Apache-2.0)

`lucene-queryparser/cases.tsv` holds every query string passed to the parser in Apache Lucene's [`TestQueryParser.java`](https://github.com/apache/lucene/blob/145d89cd30c38d25e39a0a2232cf00eee208b9cf/lucene/queryparser/src/test/org/apache/lucene/queryparser/classic/TestQueryParser.java) and [`QueryParserTestBase.java`](https://github.com/apache/lucene/blob/145d89cd30c38d25e39a0a2232cf00eee208b9cf/lucene/queryparser/src/test/org/apache/lucene/queryparser/util/QueryParserTestBase.java) at `apache/lucene@145d89cd30c38d25e39a0a2232cf00eee208b9cf` (release 10.5.2, Elasticsearch's pin), including the ones the tests expect to fail (`assertParseException`). Each line is `accept` or `reject` (what the Lucene 10.5.2 classic parser does with the string, leading wildcards allowed as in Elasticsearch), the query with `\t`, `\n`, `\r`, and `\\` escaped, and the file, line, and helper it came from. Apache License 2.0: [`lucene-queryparser/LICENSE.Apache-2.0.txt`](lucene-queryparser/LICENSE.Apache-2.0.txt), notice: [`lucene-queryparser/NOTICE.txt`](lucene-queryparser/NOTICE.txt). `crates/opentide-lucene/tests/lucene_queryparser_cases.rs` requires the engine to agree, and lists each exception with its reason.

## Kibana KQL — OpenSearch Dashboards kuery tests (Apache-2.0)

`kuery-opensearch-dashboards/cases.tsv` holds every string passed to `fromKueryExpression` or `fromLiteralExpression` in the `*.test.ts` files under [`src/plugins/data/common/opensearch_query/kuery/`](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards/tree/f04c140417a3fbb14fd8391fee1807e225f021c9/src/plugins/data/common/opensearch_query/kuery) at `opensearch-project/OpenSearch-Dashboards@f04c140417a3fbb14fd8391fee1807e225f021c9` (tag 2.19.0; the code is the Apache-2.0 Kibana 7.10.2 fork). Each line is `accept` or `reject` (whether the test expects a throw), the query as a JSON string, and the file and line it came from. Kibana's current `grammar.peggy` gives the same verdict on every case. Apache License 2.0: [`kuery-opensearch-dashboards/LICENSE.Apache-2.0.txt`](kuery-opensearch-dashboards/LICENSE.Apache-2.0.txt), notice: [`kuery-opensearch-dashboards/NOTICE.txt`](kuery-opensearch-dashboards/NOTICE.txt). `crates/opentide-kuery/tests/opensearch_dashboards_cases.rs` requires the engine to agree, and gives each accepted query with a `:` outside quotes a fault twin (the first such `:` turned into `:)`) that must error.

## Falco — falcosecurity/rules and falcosecurity/plugins (Apache-2.0)

Licence text: [`LICENSE.Apache-2.0.txt`](LICENSE.Apache-2.0.txt). `falco/<source>/<rule>.falco` is the `condition` of one Falco default rule, unmodified, written by `scripts/engine/sync_falco_catalog.py --corpus`; `<rule>.broken.falco` is a modified copy with one injected fault (an unclosed value list after the first `and`, or a leading `(`), as Apache-2.0 §4(b) asks us to state. `crates/opentide-analysis/tests/external_falco.rs` requires every public condition to come out with no finding and every twin to report `falco_parse_error`.

- `syscall/`: `rules/falco_rules.yaml`, `rules/falco-incubating_rules.yaml`, `rules/falco-sandbox_rules.yaml` from falcosecurity/rules at `e7b066bfbc8d81226ca5fa3e95ffd4dee38a2428`
- `k8s_audit/`: `plugins/k8saudit/rules/k8s_audit_rules.yaml`, `aws_cloudtrail/`: `plugins/cloudtrail/rules/aws_cloudtrail_rules.yaml`, `okta/`: `plugins/okta/rules/okta_rules.yaml`, `github/`: `plugins/github/rules/github.yaml`, `gcp_auditlog/`: `plugins/gcpaudit/rules/gcp_auditlog_rules.yaml`, from falcosecurity/plugins at `9064e9d620538aebf32912fa00f6b9ef95d46a37`

`crates/testdata/workspaces/falco/objects/rules/` holds public Falco rules converted into opentide rules (`configurations.sysdig`, sysdig-1.0); each file names the rule it comes from. Their conditions and outputs are the public text (outputs shortened in a few); the blocks add their own macros, lists, and exceptions. `crates/opentide-analysis/tests/falco_rules.rs` checks them.

## CQL — CrowdStrike/logscale-community-content (Unlicense)

`cql/<source-dir>/<slug>.cql` is one CrowdStrike Query Language query from [CrowdStrike/logscale-community-content](https://github.com/CrowdStrike/logscale-community-content) at `77cfc4e314d40611fdbc354c80ed39c9548fa12c`, unmodified. It is the decoded value of a YAML `queryString` or parser `script`, the body of a Markdown code fence, or a whole `.logscale` file. `<source-dir>` is the repository's top-level directory (`next-gen-siem/` is `Next-Gen-SIEM/`), and `-l<n>` in a slug is the query's first line when its source file holds several. [`cql/FAULTS.toml`](cql/FAULTS.toml) gives each query's source file and line. Licence: the [Unlicense](https://github.com/CrowdStrike/logscale-community-content/blob/77cfc4e314d40611fdbc354c80ed39c9548fa12c/LICENSE) (public domain dedication, <https://unlicense.org>), which `CONTRIBUTING.md` says covers all contributions.

Selection: only parts of the repository under the root Unlicense. The sub-packages that ship their own `LICENSE` (MIT: `Log-Sources/CrowdStrike/FLTR/crowdstrike-fltrcore/` and `crowdstrike-fltrlolbins/`; Apache-2.0: `Log-Sources/Airlock/`, `Microsoft/Security-Overview/`, `Imperva/CloudWAF/`, `Cisco/ASA/`, `Cisco/Meraki-Systems-Manager/`, `Palo-Alto/PAN-Firewall-Parser-Only/`, `Google/ChromeEnterpriseSecurity/`, `00-Vendor-Template/`) are left out, and so are built package zips and `Misc/falcon-query-assets-archive.zip`. The Splunk side of `CrowdStrike-Query-Language-Map/Legacy-Event-Search/` is left out. The 45 queries were picked for coverage of the language: `correlate()` with `<=>`, Falcon hunting on `ProcessRollup2`, `DnsRequest`, `NetworkConnectIP4` and `UserLogon`, Next-Gen SIEM dashboards, `case`/`match` blocks, `defineTable`, `join`, `selfJoinFilter`, `match(file=)`, regexes with named groups and flags, `array:*`, `text:*` and `ioc:lookup`, saved searches (`$falcon/investigate:...()`, `$"..."()`), `?param` and `?{param=default}`, `//` and `/* */` comments, stats shorthand `[..]`, and parser scripts (four from `Parsers-Only/`, two from `Log-Sources/`). Only queries on which the engine reports nothing at all were taken. Queries the engine flags, with a removed function such as `rdns()`, a non-breaking space, or prose in a fence, are not in the set.

`<slug>.broken.cql` is the same query with one injected fault. The fault kinds are an unbalanced `(` or `{`, a dangling `and`, a `| https://` step, a misspelt function, a misspelt parameter, a second unnamed argument, a duplicated parameter, a removed required parameter, `order=down`, an unknown regex flag, free text after an aggregate, `x := f(..., as=y)`, and `<=>` outside `correlate()`. `FAULTS.toml` records each twin's fault and the code it must report. `crates/opentide-analysis/tests/external_cql.rs` requires every public query to produce no finding (`opentide_cql::analyze` and `analyze_query`), and every twin to report its code. It also requires at least 30 pairs, every fault kind, and a manifest that matches the files.


## YARA — ReversingLabs/reversinglabs-yara-rules (MIT) and Neo23x0/signature-base (Detection Rule License 1.1)

`yara/<source>/<file>` is one public YARA rules file, unmodified, written by `scripts/sync_yara_corpus.py`. `<file>.broken.<ext>` is a modified copy with one injected fault, which libyara 4.5.4 refuses: the last rule's closing `}` removed, `$opentide_undefined or` or `opentide_undefined or` put in front of the first condition, or `condition:` misspelt `conditon:`. `crates/opentide-yara/tests/external_corpus.rs` requires every public file to produce no finding under the libyara and the YARA-X dialects, and every twin to report an error.

Selection: files libyara 4.5.4 and YARA-X 1.23.0 both compile without a warning (no external variable), under 12 KB, spread over the repositories' categories. From signature-base, only files whose every `license` meta is the DRL 1.1 and that name no other licence or copyright: rules there under CC BY-NC 4.0, the Open Government Licence, BSD, Volexity's or CAPE's licence, and collections of third-party rules without a licence meta, are left out. Nothing GPL or Elastic License is vendored.

## Exabeam Query Language — written for opentide (EUPL-1.2)

`exabeam/<name>.<profile>.exabeam` is a query written for this repository, not copied: Exabeam's own published content (ExabeamLabs/new-scale-content-hub) may not be redistributed, so it is measured locally (`crates/opentide-exabeam/tests/content_hub.rs`, `docs/EXABEAM.md`) and never vendored. The queries are realistic detections and hunts in the forms Exabeam's rules use (activity types, lists, CIDR blocks and ranges, context tables, `RGX`/`WLD` patterns, `SELECT` … `GROUP-BY`, `FOREACH`, `RGX_EXTRACT`), written with the Common Information Model's field names; `<profile>` is `rule` (a correlation-rule sequence) or `search` (a hunt). `<name>.broken.<profile>.exabeam` is the same query with one injected fault, which the specification's reference checker reports too. [`exabeam/FAULTS.toml`](exabeam/FAULTS.toml) records each twin's fault and code. `crates/opentide-analysis/tests/external_exabeam.rs` requires every query to produce no finding under its profile, every twin to report its code, and a manifest that matches the files.

## YARA-L — chronicle/detection-rules (Apache-2.0)

Licence text: [`LICENSE.Apache-2.0.txt`](LICENSE.Apache-2.0.txt). 79 community rules from `chronicle/detection-rules@a49c3752f3f013e9ead85c7430b8f39369efacbf`, unmodified, each with a `.broken.` twin (a modified copy with one injected fault). The list, and how each twin is made, is [`yaral/SOURCES.md`](yaral/SOURCES.md); `crates/opentide-yaral/tests/external_corpus.rs` requires every public rule to parse with no error but its listed exceptions, and every twin to have an error.
